PORTABLE ELECTRONIC DEVICES
Atlantic Southeast Airlines and the Federal Aviation
Administration restrict the use of certain portable
electronic devices on board the aircraft, as they can
interfere with the navigation and communication
systems on the aircraft. Please be certain that all
devices are in the "OFF" position during taxi, take off
and landing.
The following devices are permitted only at cruise
altitude when the Captain has turned off the seatbelt
sign. They should be turned off at all other times:
Personal computers and computer games
VHF scanner receivers
Tape players that do not have AM/FM capability
Video recorders
Calculators
CD players
The following devices may not be used at any time
on the aircraft:
Cellular telephones
Two-way radios (CB, Ham, or Walkie Talkie)
49 MHz transmitters
Remote controlled toys
External computer devices, such as mouse, joy
stick, or printer
AM/FM radios or TV's
Any other device which the crew suspects may
interfere with the aircraft systems
Passengers must comply with all crewmember
instructions. Atlantic Southeast Airlines appreciates
your cooperation.
